title: Creating the session-analysis report and player

interpretation.summary: This interaction turns a request for cross-harness usage statistics into an evidence-focused account of human judgment, then an interactive replay. The human sets data scope, editorial framing, cost and timing questions, and the final VCR-style experience. The agent reports finding 42 queued Claude prompts missed by its initial pass, illustrating why coverage checks must inspect harness-specific delivery formats rather than ordinary user-message records alone. Those historical collection and publication results are agent-reported in this review; the present run independently checks only its newly generated outputs.

decisions.title: Gather three harnesses and examine human steering
decisions.analysis: The opening request specifies Claude, Copilot, and Codex across two project directories, asks for turns/tokens/model mix, and explicitly seeks qualitative analysis of steering. The later response reports 42 additional genuine queued Claude inputs found by a cross-check. This supports a provenance lesson about collection, not an independently established historical total.

decisions.title: Broaden coverage to browser conversations
decisions.analysis: The human adds Claude and OpenAI browser histories and asks to expand the review. The agent reports incorporating 47 identifiable browser inputs while keeping unavailable timing and usage separate. The direction changes the evidence population rather than just the presentation.

decisions.title: Show the opening project prompt
decisions.analysis: The request to include image.png makes the project's initial framing visible in the report. The assistant reports adding it near the beginning and regenerating the PDF. The original image and PDF are not independently inspected by this review.

decisions.title: Write about judgment, not to the requester
decisions.analysis: The human rejects a second-person deliverable and asks for a project-level account of steering, judgment, and expertise grounded in evidence. The response reports a third-person rewrite covering experimental, technical, product, and editorial judgment. This is a material narrative intervention.

decisions.title: Make the resource footprint legible
decisions.analysis: The human requests harness/model cost rows and a graph. The agent distinguishes API-equivalent estimates from subscriptions and reports adding them. This review independently reprices the creation session's observed requests using the supplied frozen historical rate card, with cache and long-context adjustments. It does not claim newly verified prices or reconstruct an actual subscription bill.

decisions.title: Compare the timing of human and agent observations
decisions.analysis: The human asks when the person and agents were active. The response reports daily/hourly analysis using activity windows. Such bins describe timestamp coverage; neither the request nor the log establishes exact hands-on hours or continuous agent runtime.

decisions.title: Use comparable reports to deepen the analysis
decisions.analysis: The request asks the agent to step back and seek additional useful questions. Following the intervening approval, the agent reports adding outcome work packages and decision traces that separate completion claims from corroborated artifacts. This demonstrates delegated analytical development, not proof that every historical artifact was correct.

decisions.title: Make the clock meaningful to the reader
decisions.analysis: The human specifies Pacific time. The agent reports switching to America/Los_Angeles and checking the recorded period's PST offset. The new reviewer likewise uses an IANA timezone and date-sensitive labels instead of assuming every session has a fixed offset.

decisions.title: Turn the report into an explorable session replay
decisions.analysis: The human requests a VCR-like timeline showing what happened when and where creative bursts appeared. The agent reports a self-contained player with scrubbing, responses, markers, and clusters. Markers provide navigation through submitted directions; they are not a measured creativity score.

cost: Estimated API-equivalent total: $12.587361 USD. 176 of 176 observed requests priced. Frozen rate card dated 2026-11-07; not an actual bill.

pricing.basis: Standard global API-equivalent token processing; not actual harness subscription spend

gpt-5.4-nano.note: No writes recorded; unused write rate is ordinary input rate.

gpt-4o-mini.note: No writes recorded; unused write rate is ordinary input rate.

gpt-6-luna.note: Added for the 2026-11-08 update; standard short-context rates and the 272K long-context rule confirmed on both the model page and the standard pricing table. The 30-minute write rate is used, as for the other Codex OpenAI models.

pricing.verified_on_by_model_note: All other rates were verified on 2026-11-07; gpt-6-luna was verified on 2026-11-08.
assumptions: Reprice the frozen cohort at verified public standard global API rates, regardless of actual subscription, provider or priority tier.

Claude Code raw requests expose five-minute cache writes and standard speed; Copilot exposes 300-second Claude writes and 1800-second Sol writes. The same short-TTL policy is assumed for SQL-only Copilot records without surviving policy fields.
Use normalized request input tokens including cache read/write to test the 272000-token OpenAI threshold. Apply 2x to all input components and 1.5x to all output on qualifying requests.
Codex records do not expose cache-write TTLs (no cache writes are recorded for Codex); gpt-6-luna uses the same 30-minute write rate convention as the other OpenAI models.
No generic utility model substitution. Missing browser usage remains unpriced.
Exclude subscriptions, credits, tool fees, compute/GPU, storage, taxes, discounts, regional premiums and fast-mode premiums. This estimate does not reconstruct an invoice.
pricing.method: Inclusive input is split into fresh, cached-read and cache-write tokens. Apply the supplied model rates and long-context multipliers per request; output already includes reasoning. Estimates exclude subscriptions, tools, compute, taxes and discounts.

limitations: Observed log coverage is not a guarantee of complete project history.
Input totals include cached input; reasoning output is not counted a second time.
Metered usage is not a subscription bill or evidence of comparative model quality.

Per-input request ownership uses recorded turn IDs when available, otherwise inferred same-conversation proximity. Missing/unmatched inputs remain unattributed; turn costs cover complete recorded turns, not just elapsed playback.
Occupied bins are not working hours, runtime, latency, or proof of unattended work.
Historical assistant completion claims are agent-reported, not independently verified here.
Pasted or AI-drafted user material does not establish original authorship.
Unknown timestamps remain outside the timeline; tool payloads and internal reasoning are not displayed.
Credential redaction is best effort; private outputs require review before sharing.
